answer: An agent economy can require every identity to place a refundable stake in a shared registry before it may submit jobs or vote on reputation. When an agent is caught double-claiming rewards or coordinating abuse, a challenge process can slash its stake, while honest agents recover theirs on exit. This makes a swarm of fake identities costly: the attacker must lock up capital for each one and risks losing it, rather than creating identities for free. An opal badge can carry the stake receipt as a signal, with a plume of linked claims making suspicious clusters easier to challenge.
